notes.text: Stage 6 Pasternak uses a 1D beam/strip model. True 2D slab-on-grade plate behaviour still needs FE or a dedicated analytical plate solution.
Model interpretation is 1 m slab strip: x is the checked slab direction, b is normally 1.00 m, and outputs are per meter only when b = 1.00 m.
beta*L is below pi, so finite-beam behaviour matters. A numerical beam-on-Winkler solve is therefore used instead of relying on the infinite-beam shortcut.
Default ks derivation uses Es = E_oed and ν = 0 for consistency with the oedometric stiffness route. Switch to drained Young modulus mode if a project-specific conversion is preferred.
Pasternak shear coupling is inferred from the CPT stiffness profile as G_p ≈ eta·G_s,avg·H_p. This is a screening approximation, not a calibrated Belgian design value.
Current Pasternak inputs: G_p = 57841 kN/m, G_s,avg = 19280 kPa, H_p = 3.00 m, eta = 1.00.

Uniform full-length load on a free Winkler beam can legitimately give nearly constant settlement w ≈ q/k and almost zero bending moment. If you want edge-driven or local bending, use a patch / point load case or a 2D plate model.

notes.text: Sichardt radius of influence is shown as a screening estimate only. It is not a permit-grade hydrogeological prediction.

Hydraulic screening uses a transmissivity profile through the pumped interval: T = Σ(k_h · b). For unconfined flow, the radial drawdown is solved from the cumulative transmissivity moment rather than from one lumped k_h value.
Aquifer base was not provided, so the CPT bottom depth is used as a first-pass aquifer base. Verify this against geology or pumping-test data.
Total-stress mode does change the result here: conservative = 32.24 mm, realistic = 26.01 mm.
De Beer profile resampled from 360 raw points to 90 bins of 0.20 m.

De Beer Stage 1 (homogeneous values) implemented as q_h = q_c (identity); the diameter scale-effect is applied through the gradient limits in Stages 2 and 3. The full BGGG [4] homogeneous-conversion equations are not in the public source set.
q_b at toe is low (1797 kPa < 5 MPa) — verify the toe-level choice.
